name: nanosleep
synopsis: int nanosleep(const struct timespec *req, struct timespec *_Nullable rem);
description: nanosleep() suspends the execution of the calling thread for a specified duration with nanosecond precision. If interrupted by a signal, it returns the remaining time and can be restarted. It provides higher resolution than alternatives like sleep(3) and handles signals as per POSIX.

parameters.name: req
parameters.description: Specifies the sleep duration in seconds and nanoseconds.

parameters.name: rem
parameters.description: If not NULL, stores the remaining time if the call is interrupted.

return_value.success: Returns 0 on successful completion of the sleep
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error or interruption, and sets errno

errors.description: Problem with copying information from user space.
The pause was interrupted by a signal.
The value in the tv_nsec field was not in the range [0, 999999999] or tv_sec was negative.

bugs: If signals are received at a high rate, the remaining time may drift on successive calls; in Linux 2.4, time spent in stopped state is not counted against the interval.
